generation.explanation: Draw a line through the top vertex C that runs parallel to the bottom side AB. Where the two slanted sides cross the two parallel lines, they make alternate interior angles, which are equal. So a copy of angle A (blue) and a copy of angle B (green) fit at C, one on each side of angle C (red). The three angles now sit side by side along a straight line, and a straight line is 180°. That's why the sum is always 180°, whatever shape the triangle has. Drag the yellow corners to try it: the angles change, the sum doesn't. This only works on a flat plane. On a curved surface like a sphere, there's no single parallel line through C, so the sum can be different.
